The truth is that whenever the FAB or Navy found themselves obliged to enter an investigation into UAPs, after the inquiry, public statements were made about the investigations. epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Object resembling a flying saucer seen in Itaguaí ITAGUAÍ (O GLOBO) — Another fantastic story about a flying object that was not identified, this time in Itaguaí's skies, continues stirring public opinion. Residents are divided between believers and those skeptical of brothers José Maria Braga and José Maria Neto's account. Both say that early Saturday they saw a circular object radiating intense light and maneuvering over a mound of sun-scorched pasture grass. The large tract was temporarily lent by COPEG to cattle dealers for fattening livestock, on the Itaboraí straightaway of the Itaguaí–Santa Cruz road. The event occurred within sight of cattle tenders and sentries at Santa Cruz Air Base, only eight kilometers from the pasture. Strange object It was almost five on Saturday morning when the brothers say they saw a strange object in the pasture “radiating a light different from all colors.” Compared with moonlight, they say it “gave the night and the place a different color.” “I had just awoken,” José Neto relates, “and was driving to collect fill for the Eletrobrás power plant. My brother and I, in our truck GB 6-98-84, saw an intense light in the pasture. Out of curiosity we immediately got out to observe it closely. The strange object emitted bluish light. It was about 13 meters in diameter, with a beacon on top emitting reddish light like that of a police patrol car. “Suddenly it disappeared, making us stop apprehensively on the dirt road. We had approached about 100 meters from the original 800 separating us from the object.” José Maria Neto, known in Itaguaí as “Zé Boquinha,” is 29 and was born in Belo Horizonte. He has traveled Brazil in almost 8 years as a truck driver. His brother is an office assistant at Engenharia Noroeste, which is building the Eletrobrás power plant. His brother did not want to remain in Itaguaí yesterday so as not to have to repeat the story to friends. “I cannot say it was a flying saucer,” the driver said. “I merely told my brother that the light in the pasture at that hour could be emitted by the kind of object newspapers, radio and television keep discussing. I only know that as we approached, it emitted stronger bluish light, then, as if responding to our apprehension, switched off its lights, became a shadow in the sky and vanished. It made no noise. It rose vertically, casting its shadow. Our senses registered its presence briefly before it disappeared completely. “I do not know whether it was a flying saucer. But I felt that behind the red light emanating from its body, someone was watching our reactions.” STILL SURPRISED, JOSÉ NETO TELLS WHAT HE SAW

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Object resembling a flying saucer seen in Itaguaí ITAGUAÍ (O GLOBO) — Another fantastic story about a flying object that was not identified, this time in Itaguaí's skies, continues stirring public opinion. Residents are divided between believers and those skeptical of brothers José Maria Braga and José Maria Neto's account. Both say that early Saturday they saw a circular object radiating intense light and maneuvering over a mound of sun-scorched pasture grass. The large tract was temporarily lent by COPEG to cattle dealers for fattening livestock, on the Itaboraí straightaway of the Itaguaí–Santa Cruz road. The event occurred within sight of cattle tenders and sentries at Santa Cruz Air Base, only eight kilometers from the pasture. Strange object It was almost five on Saturday morning when the brothers say they saw a strange object in the pasture “radiating a light different from all colors.” Compared with moonlight, they say it “gave the night and the place a different color.” “I had just awoken,” José Neto relates, “and was driving to collect fill for the Eletrobrás power plant. My brother and I, in our truck GB 6-98-84, saw an intense light in the pasture. Out of curiosity we immediately got out to observe it closely. The strange object emitted bluish light. It was about 13 meters in diameter, with a beacon on top emitting reddish light like that of a police patrol car. “Suddenly it disappeared, making us stop apprehensively on the dirt road. We had approached about 100 meters from the original 800 separating us from the object.” José Maria Neto, known in Itaguaí as “Zé Boquinha,” is 29 and was born in Belo Horizonte. He has traveled Brazil in almost 8 years as a truck driver. His brother is an office assistant at Engenharia Noroeste, which is building the Eletrobrás power plant. His brother did not want to remain in Itaguaí yesterday so as not to have to repeat the story to friends. “I cannot say it was a flying saucer,” the driver said. “I merely told my brother that the light in the pasture at that hour could be emitted by the kind of object newspapers, radio and television keep discussing. I only know that as we approached, it emitted stronger bluish light, then, as if responding to our apprehension, switched off its lights, became a shadow in the sky and vanished. It made no noise. It rose vertically, casting its shadow. Our senses registered its presence briefly before it disappeared completely. “I do not know whether it was a flying saucer. But I felt that behind the red light emanating from its body, someone was watching our reactions.”

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: you were fooled
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Yesterday's early morning was quiet. Some reporters were dozing in the Central Police press room; others played cards at a corner table. The rest spoke quietly so as not to disturb anyone. No murders, robberies or incidents worth covering. Around two, the telephone rang and everyone jumped. That call might bring the big case, the day's headline. A dark-haired young man with a bow tie and glasses reached the phone first and heard: “This is Ibiúna. Something happened here. A disaster. A flying saucer landed and its occupants abducted a couple. Come quickly.” The reporter asked to be excused, covered the receiver and turned to his colleagues, sounding annoyed: “A prankster, folks. At this hour, a guy talking about flying saucers and such. What should I tell him?” Everyone hesitated. Then the oldest reporter decided to tease the caller: “Ask whether the disc turns at 78 revolutions or 45. That is the only way to stop these pranks. Scolding does not work; he will persist.” The young man did not take the suggestion. Annoyed, he hung up without further conversation. The game and the reading resumed. The matter was fading when another identical report arrived. This time the veteran decided: “Look, let's notify the newsrooms. After all, it costs nothing. With so many strange things happening, perhaps the abduction really occurred and we will be in trouble. Imagine our bosses' faces.” The warning came just in time: newspaper radio monitors had picked up a sensational broadcast about the same case. The only option was to go to Ibiúna. About a dozen journalists rushed there in several vehicles. 74 KILOMETERS LATER An hour and a half later, seventy-four kilometers from the capital, they reached the reported location. Thick fog covered the houses. Nobody was in the streets. The reporters surrounded a small taxi from São Roque carrying its driver and two young women from São Paulo. Driver Zé da Bronca was surprised by the saucer questions: “Nonsense, boys. I have been working here since last night and have not heard anything about it. I think you were fooled; it must be a prank.” He put the car in gear and drove away grinning broadly. They went to the police station, where the officer on duty also laughed incredulously: “What disc? There is not even a record player. I walked the streets until the early morning. Nobody told me about this. Last week, though, there were many rumors about strange beings, people from other worlds. Silly things from people who have nothing to do.” Somewhat disappointed, the reporters wandered to a gas station. Watchman José Anastácio, fifty-six, spoke seriously when he heard their first questions: “I heard about the abduction. But it did not happen here. It was in Feital, fifteen kilometers away, outside town.” ITCHING INSTEAD OF A DISC Next to speak was Maria Aparecida, a company employee who sang on local radio in her spare time. Arranging her hair for the photograph, she said: “It takes a fuss like this for you to show up, doesn't it? No disc at all. Someone invented it to promote Ibiúna. But nobody remembers to address the strange disease going around here. A skin disease that starts itching and becomes a sore. Our health center has been without a doctor for three months.” Aparecida's mother, Mrs. Hilda, invited them for coffee and also believed it was all rumor. She thought that if Martians, or whoever they were, came to Earth, they would seek a better place. Smiling, she said: “The only strange thing here was students looking for somewhere to escape the police during that congress.” Some saw it, but few want to talk The Central Police press-room reporters returned to São Paulo, sleepier than before the calls. Much later, newspapers decided to send others to Ibiúna to investigate flying saucers and other local phenomena. These reporters learned many things. First: flying objects resembling fireballs have been appearing on the surrounding hills. Who saw them? Respectable, sensible, educated people, residents said, naming witnesses: “Mr. Elias Fleury, owner of Fazenda Bonanza and director of an important São Paulo company. Mr. Gaze Azem Tufaile, a lawyer in the capital. Another lawyer, Mr. Sebastião Junqueira Vilella.” Speaking to them was difficult. Nobody wanted publicity, especially concerning flying saucers. They feared ridicule and misunderstanding. The journalists therefore had to speak with correspondents and local newspaper staff. Information poured in: “Something is happening, certainly. At Fazenda Bonanza, fireballs appear frequently, several times in one day. And nobody can criticize the witnesses. They are trustworthy, normal, educated people, incapable of using such a case for self-promotion.” More witnesses' names emerged: Edgar Rosa, a Sebastião, Antonio Bina. When interviewed, they described circular, luminous, somewhat yellow balls moving slowly together, not producing any noise. Edgar thought it natural, possibly caused by gas emissions from a radioactive spring. Some spoke of will-o'-the-wisps; others said Ibiúna's soil had minerals capable of producing this and other phenomena. A merchant asserted: “The same thing is happening as in Lins. There are known to be vast magnesium deposits there, emitting gases when combining with other natural elements. Then comes the glow in the air and this silly saucer talk. It is a product of the popular imagination.”

About a dozen journalists rushed there in several vehicles. 74 KILOMETERS LATER An hour and a half later, seventy-four kilometers from the capital, they reached the reported location. Thick fog covered the houses. Nobody was in the streets. The reporters surrounded a small taxi from São Roque carrying its driver and two young women from São Paulo. Driver Zé da Bronca was surprised by the saucer questions: “Nonsense, boys. I have been working here since last night and have not heard anything about it. I think you were fooled; it must be a prank.” He put the car in gear and drove away grinning broadly. They went to the police station, where the officer on duty also laughed incredulously: “What disc? There is not even a record player. I walked the streets until the early morning. Nobody told me about this. Last week, though, there were many rumors about strange beings, people from other worlds. Silly things from people who have nothing to do.” Somewhat disappointed, the reporters wandered to a gas station. Watchman José Anastácio, fifty-six, spoke seriously when he heard their first questions: “I heard about the abduction. But it did not happen here. It was in Feital, fifteen kilometers away, outside town.” ITCHING INSTEAD OF A DISC Next to speak was Maria Aparecida, a company employee who sang on local radio in her spare time. Arranging her hair for the photograph, she said: “It takes a fuss like this for you to show up, doesn't it? No disc at all. Someone invented it to promote Ibiúna. But nobody remembers to address the strange disease going around here. A skin disease that starts itching and becomes a sore. Our health center has been without a doctor for three months.” Aparecida's mother, Mrs. Hilda, invited them for coffee and also believed it was all rumor. She thought that if Martians, or whoever they were, came to Earth, they would seek a better place. Smiling, she said: “The only strange thing here was students looking for somewhere to escape the police during that congress.” Some saw it, but few want to talk The Central Police press-room reporters returned to São Paulo, sleepier than before the calls. Much later, newspapers decided to send others to Ibiúna to investigate flying saucers and other local phenomena. These reporters learned many things. First: flying objects resembling fireballs have been appearing on the surrounding hills. Who saw them? Respectable, sensible, educated people, residents said, naming witnesses: “Mr. Elias Fleury, owner of Fazenda Bonanza and director of an important São Paulo company. Mr. Gaze Azem Tufaile, a lawyer in the capital. Another lawyer, Mr. Sebastião Junqueira Vilella.” Speaking to them was difficult. Nobody wanted publicity, especially concerning flying saucers. They feared ridicule and misunderstanding. The journalists therefore had to speak with correspondents and local newspaper staff. Information poured in: “Something is happening, certainly. At Fazenda Bonanza, fireballs appear frequently, several times in one day. And nobody can criticize the witnesses. They are trustworthy, normal, educated people, incapable of using such a case for self-promotion.” More witnesses' names emerged: Edgar Rosa, a Sebastião, Antonio Bina. When interviewed, they described circular, luminous, somewhat yellow balls moving slowly together, not producing any noise. Edgar thought it natural, possibly caused by gas emissions from a radioactive spring. Some spoke of will-o'-the-wisps; others said Ibiúna's soil had minerals capable of producing this and other phenomena. A merchant asserted: “The same thing is happening as in Lins. There are known to be vast magnesium deposits there, emitting gases when combining with other natural elements. Then comes the glow in the air and this silly saucer talk. It is a product of the popular imagination.”

The object was stationary and, according to one of the pilots, located in the south of the Pelvoux massif (Ecrins massif) at the same altitude as the Pelvoux peaks and his aircraft (10,000 feet). They were then surprised to hear a detonation and immediately saw, on the left side of the road about 150 meters away, a spray of sparks 1 meter or 5 meters long at 1 meter or 1.5 meters above the ground, accompanied by a hissing and then a humming sound. Description: On October 14, 1954, around 5 PM, four witnesses observed in the south-east direction and at an altitude of 130 feet (40 meters) a spherical object moving silently but at a very high speed. The object had colors similar to a rainbow. A brief intelligence report was filed for the GEIPAN without witness statements. The description of a spherical, high-speed, multi-colored object suggests a meteor. This too-brief case is classified C due to lack of information.
Summary: Pilots reported observing a spherical object colored aluminum; likely observation of a stratospheric balloon.

Intrigued and intending to close in, the pilots gained altitude but realized it was impossible to catch up with the object. They abandoned the pursuit at 4:10 PM. Summary: Brief 2009 witness statement of an old (1965) observation from a vehicle, of "children" emerging from a saucer-shaped object in a lavender field: information lacking.
Summary: Observation of a stationary, bright triangle-shaped object in the sky: likely observation of a scientific balloon.

Description: On February 18, 1975, around midnight twenty, a witness driving on a rural road was startled by a bright spherical object moving vertically and silently oscillating across the landscape. No other witnesses were reported. Astronomical verification indicates that the Moon is near its setting in the west-northwest (azimuth 290), in the shape of a half-moon (first quarter). Description: On January 10, 1976, between 7:50 and 8:50 a.m., two individuals observed a very bright spherical object above the horizon. The witnesses noted that the object remained stationary. It gradually became invisible as the sun rose. The Gendarmerie, contacted promptly, found no object in the sky that morning or the next morning. No other testimonies were collected. Based on the collected descriptions, the witnesses likely observed a weather balloon.

Description: On January 19, 1976, around 9:30 PM, a witness exiting their home observed for 3 minutes an orange-phosphorescent disk-shaped craft approximately 2.50 meters in diameter. It appeared to be resting on a paved path along a ridge line. The witness saw the object move at a low altitude down the valley before disappearing behind farm buildings. No unusual noises were heard during the object's movement. No distinctive tracks were noted by the witness and his son at the presumed location o
Summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped craft.

Description: A witness and his grandson observed around 7:20 PM and for one minute the passage N-S of a bright green spherical object. No other testimony was collected on this phenomenon for which we lack information.
Summary: Observation of a spherical object in stationary flight then disappearance towards the East.

Description: On August 3, 1976, around 11:45 a.m., a farmer noticed in the sky the slow movement of a cylindrical object with a constant, bright aluminum color. The observation lasted 30 minutes before the object disappeared over the horizon. During the neighborhood investigation, several people identified the object's description as a promotional balloon for a tire manufacturer, seen several times that same day.
Summary: Close observation of the movement of a flying cylindrical object at 10m (33ft) above ground with a change in direction: phenomenon unexplained.

Description: On November 25, 1976, around 07:10, a farmer hunting observed a distant red glow for a few seconds, mistaking it for a chimney fire. Dominating the landscape, he then saw a sparkling light approaching him on an E-W trajectory. When it reached ten or fifteen meters from the hunter, the phenomenon changed direction, and the witness realized he was facing an elongated object about two meters long. Description: On January 14, 1977, at approximately 6:40 PM, two individuals observed a luminous, spherical object that intrigued them. The object first moved in a south-north direction, then east-west. The gendarmes observed a slowly moving, circular, luminous object with a diameter greater than that of a star in the western direction. It was visible until 9:30 PM. No other testimonies about this phenomenon were collected, and we lack information about it.

Description: In the evening of January 27, 1977, starting at 8:30 PM, two motorists observed the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon. A ball-shaped object, about the size of a soccer ball, emitted a bright white light and moved silently while oscillating on its axis. The primary witness was unable to provide any distance or speed of movement, as he observed the movement of a second light point. The witness left the scene at 9:45 PM after the phenomenon's complete disappearance. No other testi
Summary: Observations of a dark, cigar-shaped object emitting white light.

Description: On April 29, 1977, at 9:15 PM and 10:15 PM, two individuals observed the slow movement of a cigar-shaped craft. This craft emitted lights of various colors and moved parallel to the Maine. Despite a ten-minute observation, the testimonies remain brief. A third witness, located by the gendarmerie, reported a three-minute observation on the same day around 9:00 PM, describing the movement of a red ball with a "tail" that eventually "faded away." The hypothesis of an atmospheric reentr
Summary: Observation of a saucer-shaped craft.

Description: Following a local press article, two witnesses are interviewed about their observation on August 15, 1977, at approximately 00:05 of a bright, spherical object coming from the southwest. It moves slowly at a low altitude, stops for a few seconds, and then heads northeast at a higher speed. No noise was heard during the several-minute observation. No other testimony about this phenomenon, for which we have limited information, was collected.

Description: On September 23, 1977, around midnight, a person walking their dog saw in the sky for one minute two circular-shaped objects. The underside was bright white and the top side darker. The objects moved in a northeasterly-southwestern direction without making any noise. They would initiate a turn before accelerating to a high altitude and disappearing. No unexpected echoes were recorded during the night at the control tower of the Istres Air Base. No other testimonies were collected.

Description: On October 2, 1977, late in the day, a farmer was briefly overflown by a luminous spherical object in a field. Other people observed an unusual glow at the end of the field where the farmer was located. The gendarmerie, notified three days later, found no traces on the ground in the area indicated by the witnesses and no other testimony was collected that could provide further details.

Description: On October 9, 1977, at approximately 7:15 PM, two military personnel on duty observed in the sky the maneuvers of an oval-shaped object moving north-south. The object rose and fell at a slow pace, leaving a glowing trail behind it. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted between 5 and 7 minutes. A similar observation had been reported a few years earlier: at that time, it was determined to be weather balloons launched from the Istres Air Base (13).
Summary: Observation of the passage of a elongated-shaped object.

Description: On November 24, 1977, at 7:20 a.m., a witness observed the passage of an oval-shaped object, about the size of a rugby ball. It emitted a bright light and moved along an east-north trajectory before making a U-turn, retracing the same distance in the opposite direction, and disappearing behind the urban landscape. Description: On January 25, 1978, around 6:30 PM, seven children playing in the street observed the passage of an orange, oval-shaped craft. Red and white lights blinked alternately at the base of the craft. Approaching from the south, it followed a curve to head west at the same altitude as tourist planes. The children's accounts differ regarding the noise heard during the craft's passage. No other testimony regarding this probable aircraft's passage was collected.

Summary: Observation of an oval-shaped object, horizontal movement, no noise.

Description: On March 16th, around 10 PM, witnesses observed in the sky an oval-shaped object that shimmered, emitting red-orange colors. Coming from the N-E, it headed towards the S-W at a low altitude and without noise. The object disappeared, hidden by the landscape.
Summary: Observation of a rectangular-shaped object emitting a dazzling light, sudden disappearance.

Description: On May 16, 1978, at 21:15, two individuals observed in the sky a spherical object moving very quickly in a north-northwest direction. This object was of very intense luminosity. No other testimony regarding this phenomenon was collected. These witnesses likely observed the high-altitude passage of a sunlit aircraft.
Summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object with an effect on a vehicle.
Summary: Observation of the movement of a disk-shaped object.

This rectangular-shaped object was emitting a very bright light. This witness and a colleague observed the object moving at a very high speed in opposite directions twice. It moved slowly along a north-south trajectory and suddenly lifted vertically, disappearing at an extremely high speed while changing color. The object was then hidden by buildings, and when the witness found it again, he noticed a denser, rounded light in its center. The object was motionless within a glowing halo and formed a 20° angle with the ground. No other testimony was collected. At this time, the sun was
Summary: Observation of a rocket-shaped object

Description: On May 29, 1979, around 11:30 PM, a driver traveling on a rural road was surprised to see a bright orange crescent-shaped object approaching him. This low-altitude object seemed to follow the driver as he moved northwest. No noise was heard. The object disappeared from view. The following day, the witness returned to the same location and noticed the presence of the same object, but this time it was white. It disappeared behind the trees heading northwest. The sky map for that eveni

Description: On Friday, June 8, 1979, between 1:00 p.m. and 1:05 p.m., several people witnessed a peculiar phenomenon above the bay. They first observed a vertical smoke column that gradually dispersed. A few minutes later, a red-hot, spherical object traversed the sky on a straight trajectory towards the southwest with a descending curve. Moving at a relatively slow pace, the object was accompanied by white or gray smoke. The observations lasted for a few seconds without any noise being heard.
Summary: Observation of a triangular-shaped object moving slowly.

Description: On June 3, 1979, at 5:45 PM, a witness observed for 7 to 8 minutes a strange object moving from north to south in the sky. This triangular-shaped object was red in color. No noise or trail was noted by the witness. No other testimony regarding this phenomenon has been collected, for which we lack information.
Summary: Observations of silent movements across the mountainous landscape of Esterel by a very bright spherical object: probable observation of a Mylar balloon.

Description: On July 20, 1979, around 10 a.m., several people observed in the sky for approximately twenty minutes a peculiar bright object. According to the witnesses' locations, this ovoid object measured between 80 cm and 5 meters in diameter and had a metallic or black color. It was initially stationary above a house, then rose and gradually moved away without making any noise. According to the gendarmerie, no unusual observations were reported from airports or bases in the region, and no pu
Summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object spinning on itself.
Summary: Recent testimony of an old observation. Observation of a stationary triangular object of rust color. Lack of precise information.
Summary: Bright spherical object making a U-turn

Description: In September 1979, around 6:30 PM, a witness, alone outside their property, observes a bright object appearing on the horizon. This object moves very slowly in a north-south direction. Thinking it was a commercial airliner, the witness does not look away from the object. It comes to a stop above the witness, who then observes a very bright, metallic gray spherical object. After approximately one minute of being stationary, the object reverses direction, reaching the horizon in a few
Summary: Observations of the silent movement of a glowing spherical object in the sky.
Summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous triangular object.

Description: On November 15, 1979, around 7:30 a.m., a witness and his wife observed from their home a white, triangular object. This luminous object was initially stationary, then moved very slowly towards the southwest while ascending. It gradually disappeared into the air. No other testimony about this phenomenon was collected, and we have limited information about it.
Summary: Observation of a diamond-shaped craft. Abnormal behavior on sheep.
Summary: Observation of a disk-shaped object moving at very high speed

Description: On December 12, 1979, a night watchman observed in the sky an object shaped like a flying saucer, slightly rounded in the middle and tapering at the edges. The color of the object was orange. A trail of purple and orange color was visible behind the object. It suddenly disappeared at the horizon at very high speed. No other testimony about this phenomenon was collected, for which we lack information.
Summary: Observation of a triangular object changing speed and direction

Description: On December 3, 1979, at approximately 4:50 PM, two witnesses observed a triangular-shaped object emitting two red smoke trails. As it passed over a radio tower, the object stopped for a few seconds before continuing on. The witnesses followed it with their eyes until it was out of sight, with the red smoke visible until the end of the observation. A third witness observed a very bright point at the same time, but it was not possible to correlate the two observations. The investigati

Description: On December 5, 1979, at approximately 5:40 PM, a witness observed a ball-shaped object about the size of an orange with an orange reflection. It moved by spinning and alternately rising and descending. No noise was heard. The observation lasted for a quarter of an hour before the ball disappeared at a very high speed towards the southeast. The following day at the same time, the ball was visible again but changed size three times and disappeared towards the west. Another witness saw
Summary: Observation of a phosphorescent, cigar-shaped object.
Summary: Observation of a saucer-shaped craft.

Description: On January 13, 1980, around 7:10 a.m., a driver passing through the Charente-Maritime region spotted a saucer-shaped craft. Stationary, the object had a diameter of approximately 5 to 6 meters and blinking lights at its ends. Getting out of his vehicle, the witness, a customs agent, noticed that the craft was slowly moving away at about 30 to 40 km/h. What surprised the witness was that during the 5 minutes of observation, he heard no noise coming from the craft. Due to time constra
Summary: Observation of a spherical object according to the witness.

Description: On January 28, 1980, around 4:15 a.m., a witness driving a car spotted a bright object to his right. This spherical object was stationary about 40 meters above the ground and 150 meters from the witness. Orange in color, it emitted a strong light directed towards the sky. The object itself was contained within a larger, brighter circle. The witness continued on his way and noticed that the object seemed to be following him. No noise or smell was noticed by the witness, who became af

Description: On February 24, 1980, around 3:15 AM, a group of young people spotted an orange glow through the pines towards the beach. Moving to gain better visibility, they then saw a very large object heading towards the island of Yeu, which was three-quarters spherical, orange in color, and not shiny. This craft moved vertically and at a very slow and constant speed. The observation, which lasted about ten minutes, ended when the object slowly descended into the ocean, revealing a pale glow.
Summary: Observation of a disk-shaped craft. Sensation of human presence in the witness's room.

Description: On May 15, 1980, at 12:30 AM, a witness observed a luminous, oval-shaped object crossing the sky rapidly. Of a red-orange color, it was followed by a tail. The object's brightness was significantly greater than that of a star. The object disappeared while heading west. No other testimony regarding this phenomenon was collected. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.
Summary: Observation of a dome-shaped object.
Summary: Observation of a silent-moving triangular object: Lack of information.

Description: On June 19, 1980, at 11:45 PM, a child saw his room light up and spotted through the window a triangular-shaped craft. Fixed or flashing lights illuminated the object, which moved silently. The base of the craft was lit yellow, and yellow and red lights alternated on the sides, flashing as they neared the top. A red beacon lit up brightly when the side lights reached the summit. Frightened, the child called his mother, and together they watched the craft disappear into the landscape
Summary: Observation of a glowing mushroom-shaped object
Summary: Black cylindrical object with sudden acceleration

Description: On September 14, 1980, at 12:45, an air traffic controller on duty observed a peculiar phenomenon. Directly vertical to him, a black, cylindrical object was stationary. The object, located approximately 300 meters above the ground, then suddenly accelerated and disappeared heading East. No information was gathered to allow for a serious study of this observation.

Description: On September 23, 1980, at 4:15 a.m., two people returning from work spotted a flying saucer taking off behind the village church. As it ascended rapidly, it emitted bright light rays that dazzled the witnesses. One of the two people saw the craft again above a forest. No other witnesses or traces were found behind the church regarding this phenomenon, for which we have insufficient information.

Description: Old observation (1980) but recently reported (2015). During a vacation camp themed "experimental rockets" organized by CNES, a witness observes with binoculars the disappearance of a rocket named Fuch Off, which they believe was absorbed by a spherical object itself pursued by two fighter jets. This observation report is quite unusual: on the one hand, it's an old observation from 1980, declared to GEIPAN in July 2015, and on the other hand, this observation relates to a micro-rocke

Description: On December 12, 1980, around 5 a.m., a driver notices an orange light in her rearview mirror. Approximately 300 meters into the forest, an oval-shaped object emits flashing lights that change from green to red and then to blue. The witness stops to observe. The object is about 5 meters wide and 2 meters tall. Impressed, the driver continues on her way and sees the object disappear at an intersection. No further information or testimonies were collected regarding this phenomenon, for
Summary: Observation of a disk-shaped object
Summary: Multiple observations of the movements of a multicolored spherical object in the sky of Metz: lack of information.

Summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object with a change in direction.

Description: On September 22, 1981, at 6:15 a.m., a witness saw from the window of his room a flying object moving in a northwest to southeast trajectory. During the observation, which lasted one minute, the witness saw an elliptical-shaped object with blurred contours, having a kind of dome at its upper level. The object emitted a yellow-orange light. No other person in the vicinity was a witness to this appearance for which we lack information.
Summary: Observations of the movement of a cylindrical object with a silver-gray or aluminum color reflecting sunlight: probable misidentification with an airplane.
Summary: Observation of a cylindrical object over 30 meters in height.

Description: During the course of October 1981, between 11:00 PM and 1:00 AM, an individual finishes a photographic roll by taking the final shots from his parents' apartment. He photographs the city lights. Once the slides are developed by a private laboratory, he notices the presence of a peculiar bright point on one of them. Having a 13X18 enlargement printed, he then spots an object foreign to the natural setting and resembling a flying saucer. He decides to file a report with the gendarmeri

Description: On November 1, 1981, around 11 a.m., several witnesses spotted a flying object slowly heading towards the sea. This gray, cylindrical object was approximately 4 meters long. No noise was heard during the object's movement. The investigation will reveal that it was a promotional balloon launched by children from the terrace of the "Le Corbusier" building, about 300 meters from the observation location.

Description: On November 21, 1981, around 8:00 PM, two individuals observed a peculiar lighting phenomenon in the forest facing their home, which intrigued them. This rectangular-shaped object was orange-red in color and remained stationary. During the observation that lasted nearly an hour, the witnesses could see a green halo gradually surround the rectangle, followed by two very powerful lights emitting yellow light. The object slowly ascended into the air at a 45-degree angle before disappea

Summary: Observation of a triangular-shaped object moving in a zigzag pattern.

Description: At 3:00 AM on June 16, 1982, witnesses observed in the sky a spherical object with a halo, followed by a cluster of smaller points of yellow-orange color forming a glowing trail. This ensemble moved slowly in a straight line from northeast to southeast. The observation lasted less than a minute, and no noise associated with the phenomenon was heard. Based on descriptions of the phenomenon, these individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.
Summary: Observation of a disk-shaped object moving very fast
Summary: Observation of a spinning top-shaped object zigzagging.

Description: On April 25, 1983, several witnesses observed in the sky between 8:15 and 8:45 an oval-shaped object. Its color was light, almost transparent, and sometimes metallic, appearing silver. The object moved at a very low speed from west to south-southwest. Several times, it was obscured by clouds before disappearing completely. The witnesses likely observed a weather balloon, of the type used for meteorological sonding.
Summary: Observation of a spherical object with a whizzing sound.

Description: On December 8, 1983, at 11:27 PM, a witness heard a whistle similar to that produced by a glider in flight. He then saw for 5 to 6 seconds a spherical object, blue-white in color and very bright, moving horizontally. This object was followed by a trail of long orange flames. It disappeared into the landscape. No further information was gathered on this phenomenon.
Summary: Cigar-shaped object falling from the sky.

Description: On Saturday, March 24, 1984, starting at 5:50 a.m., five nuns from a convent observed a PAN in the early morning sky for 10 minutes. This oval-shaped object glowed in the night, moving very quickly from left to right and up and down. The witnesses stopped observing to resume their activities, leaving the PAN still visible in an easterly direction. This case (formerly named SARAMON (32)) is part of a series of observation cases that are currently under review (see the "Investigation

Description: On April 27, 1984, multiple witnesses reported observations above two communes in the Isère: a very bright triangular object remained stationary and could be seen for between a quarter hour and one hour and thirty-five minutes. Two witnesses observed the object's elevation and gradual disappearance after the appearance of thick smoke. No further information was collected on this phenomenon.

Description: On December 14, 1984, in the late afternoon, several witnesses in different communes and departments of France observed a bright, cigar- or ball-shaped object moving silently and quickly across the sky, leaving a trail. The observations lasted for a few seconds before the object suddenly disappeared towards the southwest. The Gendarmerie collected four testimonies from the communes of Marnans (38) and Villers-les-Luxeuil (70). However, other witnesses came forward through local pres

Description: On April 8, 1985, several witnesses observed a cone-shaped object with an irregular outline and a crimson red color plummeting vertically behind a mountain. Fearing it might be a struggling aircraft, the gendarmerie was immediately notified of the observation and also witnessed the event. The investigation will demonstrate that it was an expired marine distress rocket launched without particular intent by a resident of a nearby hamlet.
Summary: Spherical-shaped object.
Summary: Observation of a spherical object over 100 meters in size.

Description: On March 22, 1986, at approximately 6:15 a.m., a witness, while driving, observed for 7 to 8 seconds a spherical object moving from east to west. This object was blue in color on its front part and blue-green in the part that was narrowing at the back. The witness estimated the length of this object at 100 meters. No other information was gathered about this observation, which exhibits all characteristics of an atmospheric reentry.

Description: On October 6, 1986, at approximately 7:45 PM, two witnesses observed a flying object moving at a very high speed and without noise. This triangular object moved from east to west at an estimated altitude of 600 meters. No further information was collected.
Summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object moving at high speed.
Summary: Observation of a helmet-shaped object, imposing and changing direction
Summary: Observation of a cylindrical object with binoculars

Description: On the evening of July 30 to 31, 1988, around 9:30 PM, witnesses observed through binoculars a glowing cylindrical object slowly moving towards the sun. It disappeared behind clouds. No further information could be gathered.
Summary: Observation for a few seconds at night of a huge cylindrical object totally silent at an altitude of approximately 30m.
Summary: Brief observation of a triangular-shaped object.
Summary: Observation of a cylindrical-shaped craft flying over a college, 5 to 6 meters in diameter, and silent.
Summary: Observation of a triangular object with very powerful headlights that remains stationary for a minute, then departs very quickly.

Description: On May 4, 1990, at 10:30 PM, a woman observed a silent triangular object with powerful headlights that stopped for a few moments before departing at very high speed. No other information is possible on this unique testimony.
Summary: Observation of an oval-shaped object with red and green lights, moving slowly or remaining stationary.

Description: On October 26, 1990, returning from work, a witness driving their car observed a triangular object, about the size of an airplane, changing direction and moving silently. It was not possible to identify the phenomenon.

Description: On August 3, 1992, around 1 a.m., a motorist spotted, above a bank bordering a field, a white, lens-shaped mist. Located 10 meters from the vehicle and 3 meters high, the mist faded, revealing an oval-shaped, dark gray object with a transparent top that showed a human figure in a pilot's position, wearing a silver suit and a helmet. The object made no noise. Waking up his wife in the back seat, she confirmed the sighting. Suddenly, purple light beams appeared in front of and above t

Description: On October 11, 1992, between 9:30 PM and 10:30 PM, two independent witnesses observed a white, oval-shaped object moving slowly over Marseille. Both witnesses took the precaution of filming their observation. The investigations by the two brigades quickly revealed that the witnesses had observed from a distance a dirigible based in Marignagne and conducting promotional night flights. The flight data are perfectly consistent with the witnesses' description.

Description: Recent (2015) testimony of an old (1993) observation. On January 6, 1993, at 7:10 PM, three people (one adult and two children) observed above the street lamps, the silent passage of a triangular-shaped craft. Dark in color, it was illuminated by a red light in the center and several white lights grouped at each end. It suddenly took off at very high speed and disappeared behind a mountain in the direction of Annecy. Only one testimony was reported. Given the elements analyzed in th

Summary: Observation of a flash of white light and a dome-shaped object with 3 bright circles near the ground: probable observation of ground lights possibly from one or more high-lit vehicles (agricultural, 4x4).

Description: On August 13, 1993, around 9:00 AM, a witness observed from their home a stationary triangular object. The observation lasted only a few minutes and disappeared when the witness returned with their camcorder to try to film it. No aerial activity occurred at that location that day, and no other information could be gathered.

Description: On the night of September 4 to 5, 1993, around midnight, four witnesses in their vehicle observed a bright orange light, larger than a star, moving like an airplane as it approached. The observation lasted 2 to 3 minutes during which the object suddenly changed shape, becoming a very elongated diamond or a cigar-shaped object. No noise was heard. No other information could be gathered.

Description: On June 24, 1994, around 2:40 a.m., during a night patrol, the attention of three gendarmes was drawn to lights above the highway. As they approached, they realized these lights were coming from a stationary triangular object at an unspecified distance from the ground. After stopping their vehicle, the object gently approached and hovered above the gendarmes' car. When they started driving again, the object suddenly accelerated, becoming just a point in the sky. Without being able t
Summary: Observation of 3 triangular or pyramid-shaped objects flying over the witness's car at low altitude

Description: On June 27, 1994, around 11:00 a.m., a witness driving a car observed at a distance estimated at 8 km (5 miles) two dark, pyramid-shaped objects, without any lights or indicators, remaining stationary. As the witness turned a corner, he lost sight of the two phenomena. A short distance later, he encountered a third black triangular object flying above his car at the same speed, approximately 80 km/h (50 mph). Summary: Daytime observation of the silent movement of a cylindrical object associated with two round, metallic-colored shapes moving in all directions: probable observation of a balloon.
Summary: Observation of a cylinder-shaped craft.

Description: On October 1, 1995, around 2:45 a.m., a witness observed a cylindrical object of aluminum color while driving. For one minute, he observed a strong orange light coming from a cylinder approximately 1 meter in diameter. No noise was noticed. No other information could be gathered.
Summary: Observation of a cylindrical object

Description: On the night of July 3rd to 4th, 1997 at 4:00 a.m., a witness observing from the deck of their sailboat saw a bright light descend rapidly for 2 to 3 seconds, stabilize for a moment, then quickly depart horizontally and disappear in approximately 2 to 3 seconds. The witness called their two sleeping crewmates to share their observation when they witnessed a second phenomenon, a yellow ocher diamond-shaped object with lights on its peaks. Summary: Observation of the very slow passage of a very large triangular object: lack of information.

Description: Recent (2014) testimony of an old observation (summer 1998 - the exact date is not given; we arbitrarily date it to 01). In July or August 1998, a young boy was playing with another child on a property in the middle of the countryside near CHATEL-MONTAGNE (Allier). Their attention was drawn to a elongated object, gray in color, with (indeterminate number of) portholes that allowed white light from inside to pass through. The object appeared to the right of a chalet directly in front

Description: On the night of August 7 to 8, 1999, between 11:30 PM and 1:30 AM, an amateur astronomer observing the Andromeda galaxy noticed with the naked eye an object moving at a constant speed on a North-South trajectory. After a few moments, the trajectory suddenly changed direction, shifting to North-Northwest before returning to North. The observed phenomenon was silent, not luminous, with a brown-maroon color. The sketch made by the witness depicts a barrel-shaped object. The observation

Description: On June 27, 2000, around 11 PM, several witnesses observed the passage of objects with lights of various colors flying over houses. Trajectories varied depending on the point of observation. Although witnesses described them as flying saucers, it is likely these observations were of Mirage 2000s performing maneuvers in the area until 2 AM.

Description: On August 1, 2000 at 1:20 AM, two people from an apartment observed in the sky a green, oval-shaped object moving very quickly to the southeast on a straight trajectory. The observation lasted 6 seconds before the object split into two parts and was hidden by the urban landscape. No other testimony about this phenomenon was collected. Based on the given indications, these people likely observed an atmospheric reentry.

Description: On November 11, 2000, a witness observed a disk-shaped craft with three legs. This craft flew quickly at low altitude without making a sound. A similar observation was made by a gendarme who reported a motor noise. The investigation conducted by the gendarmerie will show that it was the test flight of a ULM (Ultra Light Motorized Aircraft) prototype intended for filming birds and for the filming of the movie "Le Peuple migrateur" (The Migrating People).
Summary: Observation of a bright cylindrical object moving slowly.

Description: On June 24, 2001, around 7 PM, a witness observed a vertical cylindrical object moving slowly. The witness filmed the phenomenon by following it on a motorcycle to get a better view of its movements. The estimated altitude of the object was 600 meters, and it appeared to be 15 meters tall with a diameter of 2.5 meters. It was colored aluminum with bright points like headlights. The movement was slow, estimated at approximately 10 km/h. The investigation was unable to identify this o

Description: On the night of September 26 to 27 at 2:14 AM, a witness observed for 7 to 10 seconds the rapid passage of a large triangular object. This object, which appears much larger than an airplane, moves silently and very quickly, about 2 to 3 times faster than an airplane at an estimated altitude of 600 to 700 meters. The triangular shape was dark, with a phosphorescent light at each end. No explanation could be given for this phenomenon.

Description: On February 2, 2002, around 7:40 PM, a family in a car observed, above a forested area, an illuminated disk-shaped object. During the night, this object, topped with a dome, was gray in color with spaced-out white lights around its belt. The phenomenon remained stationary above the trees, with an estimated diameter of about 15 meters by the witnesses. No unusual noises were heard. After a change in the road axis, the witnesses lost sight of the object. At the time, the case was clas
Summary: Observation of the silent passage of a brown cylindrical object: lack of information.
Summary: Observation of a triangle-shaped object with lights at the vertices

Description: On October 29, 2002, around 7 PM, a witness observed a triangle-shaped object with apparent dimensions of 40 to 50 cm, having lights at its vertices, moving at a constant speed along a straight trajectory and making no noise. No further information could be gathered on this classified C report.
Summary: Observation of a large triangular object, with 9 orange-colored rings

Description: On February 5, 2003, at approximately 6:50 PM, a witness observed a large triangular object with 9 orange rings. The shape emitted a faint airplane noise; the weather was cloudy. After remaining stationary for a few seconds, the phenomenon turned 45 degrees and ascended on a trajectory, then disappeared. Unexplained phenomenon classified as D.

Description: Recent testimony (03/10/2012) of an old observation whose date remains approximate according to the witness. On September 15, 2003, around 9:30 PM, an individual observes the successive presence in the sky of two dark, triangular objects equipped with several lights. Initially stationary, they then move rapidly with changes in direction and disappear towards the setting sun. No noise is heard during the observation. The witness illustrates his account with a photo of the Petit-Recha
Summary: Cylindrical object taking off from a property.
Summary: Observation of the passage of a boomerang-shaped object.
Summary: Observation of the movement of a boomerang-shaped object.

Description: Recent testimony of an old observation: A witness observes in April 2006 at 10 a.m. (the exact date is not specified, a arbitrary date is given here) the silent and straight movement of a black object in the sky. The speed is constant and the object disappears on the horizon. The witness compares the object to a "barrel of oil" or a "black cabin." Description: On June 12, 2007, around 10:30 PM, two witnesses at home heard a deafening noise for 10 minutes but did not see anything through their windows. At exactly 12:08 AM, the same rumbling was heard and one witness saw for 5 seconds a gray triangular object with colored lights. The object flew at very low altitude in a specific direction. Description: On October 2, 2007, around 1:00 PM, a witness in their garden noticed in the sky a particular phenomenon: a large, diamond-shaped object of several colors flying silently at low altitude. Intrigued, this witness decides to follow the phenomenon in a car for 5 to 6 km between Neuville-les-Dames and Vonnas. Summary: Observation of a pyramid-shaped object at five meters from the ground. High-pitched voices and incomprehensible words heard; severe headaches: lack of information and cross-references.

Summary: Observations of a black spherical object with gray tubes below; initially stationary, then slow movement towards the West on a straight trajectory at the same altitude in the sky: mistaken for a public promotional festive balloon.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: **Case Summary: Unidentified Flying Object (UFO) Observation** The GEIPAN (Investigator) has concluded the examination of several cases pending classification. He publishes a synthesis with available data from both witness testimonies and investigations at the time (see attached document). A witness and his son, driving around 5:15 PM, observed an unusual "long and pointed sky phenomenon" with their binoculars. The witness stopped and observed the PAN with 8x25 binoculars, but no further details were visible. Upon arriving home, the witness attempted to locate the PAN with 12x50 binoculars and found two static, triangular objects, but darker this time. The objects were eventually obscured by clouds around 6:00 PM. The witness provided a detailed account of his observation to the GEIPAN. Only one testimony was collected on these phenomena. The witness seems to describe two distinct types of __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s: 1. "A... unusual light phenomenon (long and pointed towards the sky) to the southwest (from Cholet) at about 20° from the ground and approximately 1 degree high." 2. "B... two invisible to the naked eye (apparently static) triangular objects, dark this time (I believe these are the same as the first, farther away, with a different orientation, i.e., not facing the sun)." The second phase includes a reconstructed photograph depicting the scene, showing the two __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s as inverted "V" shapes with a point at their base, positioned slightly offset in height and azimuth (see attached document). The witness stated that the first PAN was white and "blindingly bright" (like a streetlamp in broad daylight), while the second was darker. No movement of these objects was observed by the witness. In response to the question about trails or halos, the witness interestingly noted, "The two descending branches of the triangle resembled airplane trails (but usually, they are parallel, and an airplane always evolves in the sky, even if it's first on the horizon)." The witness thus considered simple airplane trails but dismissed the hypothesis based on his knowledge of these phenomena. However, airplane trails are not always parallel. In a very stable atmosphere (little or no wind, low humidity), they can be very short and, depending on the number (bi-jet), the arrangement of the aircraft's engines, and the turbulence they generate, they can diverge as they exit the fuselage (see example #4 in the attached document). The dark color likely resembles example #15 in the document. It is typical of trail observations during twilight: the sun has been down for a few minutes, the sky is still clear, and according to the position of the terminator (a fictional line marking the boundary between the sunlit and shadowed areas of the Earth), these trails can take on colors ranging from white to gray/black, through yellow, orange, and even red. The first PAN observed earlier (5:15 PM) was very likely a persistent condensation trail from an airplane passing through a temporarily wetter area at high altitude, still well-lit by the sun, which, observed from Cholet, set three minutes later at 5:18 PM on November 24, 2016. The contrast with surrounding darker clouds gives the impression of "blinding brightness." It's possible that one of the later observed trails came from the same airplane as the first, though it's difficult to prove. The immobility of these __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s can be explained by two factors: - For the first one, since it's likely a persistent condensation trail, for as long as wind at high altitude remains light, it can persist in place or almost, for a relatively long time. - For the seconds, two parameters come into play: a. The involved airplanes are probably very far and high (the witness stated the __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s were invisible to the naked eye and low on the horizon), so their movement is apparently slow and may be imperceptible, at least over a short time and in a clear sky, which wasn't the case here. b. The witness mentioned that many clouds were present and moving quickly (so relatively low), which prevents the witness from perceiving the slow movement of the airplanes and their trails, which are also regularly obscured. The only seemingly contradictory element, at least for the second __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s, is the duration of observation, as the witness stated, "continuously from 5:30 PM to 6:00 PM." Given that they were observed from very far and low on the horizon, it seems challenging to envision airplanes being observed for so long, especially without the witness eventually perceiving their movement. At 5:30 PM, the sun was at 1°36 below the horizon and at an azimuth of 241°, i.e., southwest, just like the __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s (verified from the photo provided by the witness). Therefore, situated in the same direction as the sun while being very far from the witness, the condensation trails from the implicated airplanes should, in all logic, still be illuminated by the sun and exhibit a white or orange coloration, not a dark one if they were observed as early as 5:30 PM. For these trails to appear dark, it's essential they are no longer illuminated by the sun, especially if they are in the same azimuth as it. Thus, the only possibility is that the beginning of observation of the last two __UFO_PROTECTED_001__s started much later than 5:30 PM; it could thus have been shorter and more compatible with the hypothesis. The GEIPAN classifies the case as "B: Misidentification with Airplane Condensation Trails."

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: At about 3:50 PM on Feb. 09,I observed an oblong, cylinder shaped object moving slowly from the NNE to the SSW. I at first believed it was a passenger jet as the local airport is nearby and the area occupied by the object is frequently used by approaching planes.Exiting the US127 N. highway onto the I-69 W. interchange ramp I pulled over to observe the object as something appeared "wrong" with what I was seeing.The object appeared about as large as say a DC-9 jet, but upon further observation I discovered the object displayed no wings nor did it have a vertical tail section.The object was a brilliant, "clean" white with no apparent projections from its body.It moved more slowly than what is typically seen from planes approaching the local airport for landing.It flew in an apparent straight line with no visible or apparent altitude changes.After watching it for a few minutes the crafts aspect began to narrow as it apparently maneuvered to a more westerly path.As the object turned to where it would be seen only from behind, it could no longer be seen-it just disappeared.To confirm my own suspicions, I drove several miles West down I-69 to attempt to regain visual contact with the object but never saw it again.I believe it was originally flying slowly enough that I could have regained visual contact with it, assuming it maintained a similar speed and made no radical course changes.Interestingly, I don't think any of the other motorists driving by that day noticed anything strange about the object.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: i was riding in a car back in about 1982-83, crossing over a bridge in my home town of frankfort, new york. it was a clear summer day. i noticed a reflection in the sky to my left. i looked over and upward and saw a flying disc in the sky. it was moving in such a way as to not be hindered by gravity, momentum or inertia, moving as easily and quickly as shining a flashlight on a nearby wall. the craft was flying towards a cessna aircraf'ts windshield. it moved forward and back. it was extremely close at times. the aircraft's pilot reacted by diving the plane and trying to avoid a mid air collision. this game went on for several seconds as my mom aunt and i observed. it was pretty horrific watching this. the craft, as i call it, had a sort of pulsation coming from it. kind of like an unknown power system was engaged. i don't remember seeing any ionization. i saw the craft clearly. it was silver or almost bare metal in color. it was bigger than the aircraft. i saw it from the side as it never turned on its side. i assume it was round, but don't know for sure. i knew in my head that what i was seeing must be what many people had said a ufo or flying saucer must be. i'm now 37 years old and have been wondering if we can find the occupant or occupants in the airplane. now, that would be a real interesting interview at the other end of the sighting.
